name: Jammu & Kashmir
soilDescription: Thin, immature mountain soils on steep slopes, rich in organic litter but low in depth.

name: Punjab
soilDescription: Deep, fertile alluvium laid down by the Sutlej and Beas — the backbone of India's wheat belt.

name: Himachal Pradesh
soilDescription: Podzolic hill soils, acidic and humus-rich, suited to orchards and terraced cropping.

name: Uttarakhand
soilDescription: Himalayan foothill soils, thin on the ridges and alluvial-rich in the Terai valleys.

name: Rajasthan
soilDescription: Arid, low-humus desert soils with poor water retention, punctuated by fertile irrigated pockets.

name: Uttar Pradesh
soilDescription: Gangetic alluvium — among the most fertile soil in the world, renewed yearly by river silt.

name: Bihar
soilDescription: Flood-plain alluvium from the Ganga, rich in minerals but prone to seasonal waterlogging.

name: Assam
soilDescription: Brahmaputra alluvium, acidic and humus-rich, ideal for tea and paddy cultivation.

name: Gujarat
soilDescription: Regur (black cotton) soil across Saurashtra, high in clay and moisture-retaining capacity.

name: Madhya Pradesh
soilDescription: Deccan trap-derived black soil across the Malwa plateau, excellent for cotton and soybean.

name: Jharkhand
soilDescription: Iron-rich red soil over the Chota Nagpur plateau, coarse-textured and moderately fertile.

name: West Bengal
soilDescription: Deltaic alluvium of the Ganga-Brahmaputra delta, among the most intensively cropped soils in India.

name: Maharashtra
soilDescription: Deccan black soil across the plateau interior, prized for cotton; laterite along the Konkan coast.

name: Chhattisgarh
soilDescription: Red and yellow soils of the Chhattisgarh basin, rice being the dominant crop despite modest fertility.

name: Odisha
soilDescription: Red lateritic uplands transitioning to fertile coastal alluvium near the Mahanadi delta.

name: Goa
soilDescription: Iron- and aluminium-rich laterite typical of the humid Western Ghats coastline.

name: Karnataka
soilDescription: Red sandy loam across the Deccan plateau, with black soil in the north and laterite on the coast.

name: Telangana
soilDescription: Red chalka and black regur soils over granite terrain, suited to millets and cotton.

name: Andhra Pradesh
soilDescription: Red soils inland giving way to fertile deltaic alluvium along the Krishna-Godavari coast.

name: Kerala
soilDescription: Deep laterite soils under heavy monsoon rainfall, well suited to spices, coconut and rubber.

name: Tamil Nadu
soilDescription: Red loamy soils over the interior plateau with fertile alluvium along the Cauvery delta.
